name: Signaling Principle
fact: The effect of the signaling principle (using cues to highlight essential information) on learning outcomes is contested: one study found no significant effect of signaling, while another found the strongest cue type (an embodied pedagogical agent) outperformed other cue groups.
boundary: The effect of signaling is not universally observed across all studies, with some research finding no significant impact on learning performance.

provenance.title: Hybridising Signaling Principle And Nielsen’s Design Guidelines In A Mobile Application
provenance.quote_or_locus: Most current research on mobile learning applications pays little attention to multimedia principles, especially the Signalling principle, to improve user interaction

provenance.title: On the role of working memory capacity and signaling in multimedia learning.
provenance.quote_or_locus: No effect of signaling was observed

provenance.title: Unpacking the Role of Embodied Pedagogical Agents in Multimedia Learning: Beyond Attention Guidance
provenance.quote_or_locus: the embodied pedagogical agent group achieved the best learning outcomes, surpassing all other cue groups
